title: Characteristic-coordinate realization of a cubical relation poset
statement:
Use ordinary nerves and geometric realization with the quotient topology of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $n\geq0$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. Write $F_{n,i}$ for the inclusion poset of subsets $U\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$ containing $i$, and $D_{n,i}$ for the poset of pairs $(U,V)\in F_{n,i}\times F_{n,i}$ such that $U\cap\{i+1,\ldots,n\}=V\cap\{i+1,\ldots,n\}$, ordered by inclusion in both entries. Give
$$T_{n,i}=\{(p,q)\in[0,1]^{n+1}\times[0,1]^{n+1}:p_i=q_i=1,\ p_j=q_j\text{ for every }j>i\}$$
the subspace topology inherited from the finite real coordinate space. For a subset $U$, let $\chi_U$ be its characteristic vector. The formula on a realized chain of pairs with barycentric weights $w_a$,
$$[(U_0,V_0)\subseteq\cdots\subseteq(U_r,V_r);(w_0,\ldots,w_r)]\longmapsto\left(\sum_{a=0}^r w_a\chi_{U_a},\sum_{a=0}^r w_a\chi_{V_a}\right),$$
is well-defined and is a homeomorphism $|N(D_{n,i})|\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{n,i}$. If $c_{n,i}:|N(F_{n,i})|\to[0,1]^{n+1}$ is given by $[U_\bullet;w]\mapsto\sum_a w_a\chi_{U_a}$, its composites with the realizations of the two poset projections $D_{n,i}\to F_{n,i}$ are exactly the two coordinate projections of this homeomorphism.

source.place: Section 2.2.2, explicit cubical quotient immediately before Remark 2.2.2.6, printed p.76 (PDF p.94); agent expansion of the relation-space comparison implicit in passage to geometric realization. No Stacks tag states this finite cubical triangulation.

proof.text: Put $J=(\{L,R\}\times\{0,\ldots,i-1\})\amalg\{i+1,\ldots,n\}$, of cardinality $m=n+i$. Encode $(U,V)\in D_{n,i}$ by $W\subseteq J$: $(L,j)\in W$ means $j\in U$, $(R,j)\in W$ means $j\in V$, and a tail label $j$ belongs to $W$ exactly when $j\in U\cap V$. The inverse inserts $i$ in both sets, assigns the left and right labels separately, and inserts each tail label in both. These formulas are mutually inverse and preserve inclusion. Similarly $T_{n,i}$ has independent coordinates $x_{L,j}=p_j$, $x_{R,j}=q_j$ for $j<i$ and $x_j=p_j=q_j$ for $j>i$; reinserting the two constant coordinates $1$ and copying each tail coordinate gives its inverse. Both coordinate maps are continuous in the displayed subspace topologies. In this notation the proposed map is $H([W_\bullet;w])=\sum_a w_a\chi_{W_a}$ followed by this explicit coordinate insertion.

proof.text:
For any monotone $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$, the nerve operator restricts a chain to $W_{\alpha(0)},\ldots,W_{\alpha(s)}$. The coordinate identity
$$\sum_{b=0}^{s}t_b\chi_{W_{\alpha(b)}}=\sum_{a=0}^{r}\left(\sum_{\alpha(b)=a}t_b\right)\chi_{W_a}$$
is exactly the realization identification of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus $H$ is well-defined on the quotient, including zero weights and repetitions. Each simplex map is a finite sum of scalar multiples of fixed real vectors, hence continuous, so the quotient topology makes $H$ continuous. Nonnegative weights with sum $1$ give coordinates in $[0,1]$; after coordinate insertion they have $p_i=q_i=1$ and equal tails, as required.

proof.text:
Let $x\in[0,1]^J$. For $m>0$, choose an enumeration $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m$ of $J$ with $x_{\sigma_1}\geq\cdots\geq x_{\sigma_m}$. Set $W_0=\varnothing$, $W_k=\{\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k\}$ and
$$w_0=1-x_{\sigma_1},\quad w_k=x_{\sigma_k}-x_{\sigma_{k+1}}\ (1\leq k<m),\quad w_m=x_{\sigma_m}.$$
These weights are nonnegative and sum to $1$. They specify a realization point by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its coordinate at $\sigma_j$ is $\sum_{k=j}^{m}w_k=x_{\sigma_j}$, so $H$ is surjective. When $m=0$, use the single vertex $W_0=\varnothing$ with weight $1$; both its coordinate cube and its realization are singletons. This also covers $n=i=0$.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-realization-cw-subcomplex], a realization point has a unique nondegenerate chain with positive weights. For a nerve of an inclusion poset, nondegenerate means a strictly increasing chain: an adjacent repetition is a degeneracy, and a degeneracy repeats a vertex. Write this chain $W_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq W_r$. The coordinates of its image are $1$ on $W_0$, $0$ outside $W_r$, and $s_a=\sum_{b=a}^{r}w_b$ on $W_a\setminus W_{a-1}$ for $1\leq a\leq r$. If $r>0$, every difference is nonempty and $1>s_1>\cdots>s_r>0$. Thus the image recovers these groups as its distinct intermediate coordinate levels, recovers $W_0$ as the coordinates equal to $1$, and recovers every $W_a$ by adjoining the groups in decreasing-level order. It recovers the weights as $w_0=1-s_1$, $w_a=s_a-s_{a+1}$ for $1\leq a<r$, and $w_r=s_r$. If there are no intermediate levels, $r=0$, the image is the characteristic vector of $W_0$ and the sole weight is $1$. Hence image coordinates determine the positive representative uniquely, so $H$ is injective. In particular ties in step 3 give the same point, and zero endpoint weights cause no ambiguity.

proof.text: For each enumeration $\sigma$ of $J$, let $C_\sigma=\{x\in[0,1]^J:x_{\sigma_1}\geq\cdots\geq x_{\sigma_m}\}$. These finitely many closed sets cover the cube. On $C_\sigma$ the weights in step 3 depend continuously on $x$, and the chain $W_\bullet$ is fixed, so the characteristic simplex map of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] makes the inverse $I_\sigma:C_\sigma\to|N(D_{n,i})|$ continuous (interpreting $W_k$ by step 1). Steps 3 and 4 show these maps all equal the set-theoretic inverse of $H$ on their domains. To check continuity of the assembled inverse, let $B$ be any closed subset of the realization. Its inverse image is $\bigcup_\sigma I_\sigma^{-1}(B)$. Each term is closed in $C_\sigma$, hence closed in the cube since $C_\sigma$ is closed; the union is finite, hence closed. Thus the inverse is continuous. For $m=0$ it is the constant characteristic map of the single vertex. Combining with the coordinate insertion of step 1 proves the required homeomorphism for the ordinary subspace topology.

proof.text: The same identity in step 2, applied to a chain of single subsets, makes $c_{n,i}$ well-defined and continuous. The nerve of the first poset projection sends $[(U_a,V_a)_a;w]$ to $[(U_a)_a;w]$ and the second sends it to $[(V_a)_a;w]$, by the nerve and realization formulas of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Therefore their composites with $c_{n,i}$ are respectively $\sum_a w_a\chi_{U_a}$ and $\sum_a w_a\chi_{V_a}$, exactly the two components of $H$ after coordinate insertion. These equalities hold on every quotient representative, proving both projection compatibilities.
